newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian centre-right denounce Prodi's mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian centre-right denounce Prodi's mini-budget.

text.p: Italy's centre-right opposition bloc promised to fight the government's mini-budget, saying the package would harm state accounts.
"This will weigh on (public) finances in the years to come. It's a real timebomb," said Antonio Marzano, vice-chairman of former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Forza Italia party.
Pierferdinando Casini, leader of the centrist CCD party, was equally damning: "It is worse than all our expectations."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the budget, approved by his cabinet earlier on Thursday, would cut 15.5 trillion lire ($9.2 billion) off the 1997 deficit.
The package is based on a mix of accountancy and fiscal changes, with much of the cash coming from advance tax payments.

The centre-right Freedom Alliance boycotted the parliamentary vote on the 1997 budget when it was debated at the end of last year. "We won't do the same this time," CCD chairman Clemente Mastella said.
However the bloc was divided over whether to organise public demonstrations against the budget.

"Protests risk reinforcing the government bloc," Casini said. Maurizio Gasparri, a leading figure in the hardright National Alliance party, said the opposition would call for street protests. "The time and place will be decided in the future," he told reporters. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501 ($ = 1677 Italian Lire)
